generation.hypothesis: A lightweight and superior comprehensive performance material can be designed by combining the principles of high-entropy alloys, precipitation strengthening, and grain refinement.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy with a single BCC solid solution
generation.intervention: Addition of precipitation-strengthening particles and grain refinement through powder metallurgy or selective laser melting
generation.mechanism: Precipitation strengthening, grain refinement strengthening, and solid solution strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved compressive strength, thermal stability, and resistance to radiation damage
generation.baseline: Traditional superalloys and arc-melted high-entropy alloys
generation.boundary: Limitations of current thermodynamic databases and the need for further study on mechanical properties
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the prediction of material behavior under extreme irradiation environments and the effect of composition changes on mechanical strength

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of the mechanical properties of the designed material with traditional superalloys and arc-melted high-entropy alloys under high-temperature structural applications
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the designed material does not exhibit improved compressive strength, thermal stability, and resistance to radiation damage compared to traditional superalloys and arc-melted high-entropy alloys, the hypothesis is falsified.

System: Quinary W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA with compositions W29.4Ta42Cr5.0V16.1Hf7.5 (thin film) and W31Ta34Cr5.0V27Hf3.0 (thick film). Processing: Magnetron-sputtering deposition from metal targets (99.99% purity) at room temperature and 3 mTorr pressure with no bias voltage; power settings: W (200 W), Ta (400 W), Cr (50 W), V (350 W), Hf (25 W); film thicknesses: 100 nm (thin) and 3 µm (thick). Question: Can a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy be successfully fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) despite processing challenges, and how do its microstructure, hardness, and corrosion resistance compare to traditional superalloys and arc-melted counterparts?. System: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal equiatomic composition of Nb, Mo, Ta, W powders with 99.9% purity). Processing: Selective laser melting (SLM) using FORWEDO LM120 equipment with a 500 W fiber laser in an argon atmosphere (<20 ppm oxygen); parameters included hatch distance 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.1 mm, laser power factor 0.8, scanning velocity 250 mm/s, and a triple-pass remelting strategy (3x energy input) to achieve a linear energy density of 2.83 J/mm. Question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases). Processing: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700 °C) at a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD and TEM characterization.
